messages:
maya: FYI noticed a p99 regression (~8-12%) on 512-token requests after we enabled the new coalesce jitter logic in the continuous-batching path. numbers from last night: p50 steady, p95 ~+3%, p99 spiked.

oliver: ugh. timing? which branch/config did you flip? :thinking: 

maya: rolled runtime change that sets coalesce_delay_ms=2, microbatch_interval_us=800, coalesce_jitter=0.03 and enabled the size-based queue gating.

perf-bot: deploy r1782 to staging completed @1782345690

maya: attached a quick perf snippet from staging profiler (shortened):
```
seq=512, batch_mean=16 -> p99 320ms (prev 285ms)
gpu_util 64% -> 68%
kernel_choice: flash_attn fallback increased by 22%
kv_cache_hit_rate 0.82 -> 0.75
avg_coalesce_wait 5.1ms
```

sana: kernel fallback up is interesting. are we changing kernel selection thresholds based on microbatch sizes? coalesce jitter could be producing more ragged seq groups causing non-optimal kernel picks.

oliver: yeah if batches become more heterogeneous due to jitter we might trigger different kernels. can you dump per-batch seq hist and kernel id? also check if KV cache sharding alignment changed — that could drop hits.

maya: here's the quick log of batch shapes (truncated):
```
[16 x 512], [8 x 128], [24 x 256], [5 x 1024], ...
kernel_ids: [1,1,2,3,...] // 3 = fallback kernel
```

tony: I suspect coalesce_jitter=0.03 is too aggressive for this workload mix. jitter is causing microbatches to span very different token lengths which explodes kernel selection variance. propose lowering jitter to 0.005 and increasing microbatch_interval_us to 1200 to let small requests coalesce more predictably.

sana: also try token_budget_target per-priority. small-req-heavy routes should use token_budget_target=12000 while long-context routes keep 30000. that keeps gates from filling with long seqs.

oliver: +1. and switch queue policy to size-prefer (prefer similar seq lengths) rather than strict FIFO for these routes. we already have an experimental policy: gating_mode="length_bucket".

maya: I ran a quick A/B on staging: A (current): coalesce_jitter=0.03, microbatch_uv=800; B (tweaks): jitter=0.005, microbatch_uv=1200, gating_mode=length_bucket, token_budget_target=12000. Results after 1h synthetic traffic:
- A: p99 318ms
- B: p99 292ms
kv_cache_hit_rate B: 0.81 (was 0.75)
kernel fallback B reduced by 15%

sana: nice improvement. can you share the exact config snippet you used for B? will try locally.

maya: config B:
```
continuous_batching:
  microbatch_interval_us: 1200
  coalesce_delay_ms: 2
  coalesce_jitter: 0.005
  gating_mode: length_bucket
  token_budget_target: 12000
```

oliver: let's also add a tiny hysteresis for bucket boundaries so a request doesn't flip buckets if its token length is within +/- 4 tokens.

tony: noted. I'll run a longer 12h run overnight for both A and B with production traffic sampling and capture kernel traces + KV cache shard logs. will also run the --trace-kernels flag.

maya: opened a short issue with links to profiler dumps and comparison graphs: https://redwood.internal/ops/issue/INF-821 (brief)

perf-bot: scheduled perf-run job 1782345900 on infra-perf

sana: action items:
- tony: kernel traces + 12h run (due tomorrow morning)
- oliver: add hysteresis to length_bucket logic and create small change PR
- maya: roll B config to a small canary in prod for the /embed route only

oliver: i'll also add a metric for per-batch kernel_id distribution to make regressions obvious in alerting.

maya: thanks all. if B looks stable we'll make B the default and add a config knob per-route to opt into higher jitter for latency-insensitive workloads. :white_check_mark:

tony: starting runs now, will post summary when done.

maya: last note — keep an eye on model-quantization paths too. fallback kernel changes sometimes correlate with a quantized matmul path being selected; we should mark that in traces.

sana: agreed. let's reconvene with results tomorrow.
